question: Estimate Punctual Pros revenue from public filings
html:
Punctual Pros revenue estimate

Public filings support FY2025 pro forma revenue of about $22M est. (range $16–28M). Pennsylvania contributes roughly $18M est. and New Jersey (the Horvath add-on) about $3–5M est. Confidence is medium (Punctual Pros public filings).

How the estimate is built

  • PPP base: The Rohrer Company's April 2020 PPP loan was $745,985. That implies about $3.58M of 2019 payroll, with high confidence. It also implies about 50–58 employees and about $9–12M of 2019 revenue est. (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Horvath base: A $251,894 PPP loan implies about $1.21M of payroll, about 19–22 employees and about $3–4M of 2019 revenue est. (Punctual Pros public filings).
  • Labor cross-check: About 113 employees at 2024 Lancaster wages (~$76K) and a 40–45% labor ratio imply an $18–22M PA run-rate est. at the BSP purchase on Apr 3, 2024. The 113 headcount comes from a task brief and has not been re-verified (BSP firm profile).
  • Franchise disclosure cross-check: The 2026 franchisee lists show 25 territories, with high confidence. Mapping them to Item 19 quartiles gives about $12–19M for PA and $3–5M for NJ (Punctual Pros public filings).

Territory and estimate summary

MetricEstimateConfidence
Territories (PA / NJ)19 / 6High
FY2025 PA revenue~$18M est. ($12–24M)Medium
FY2025 total incl. NJ~$22M est. ($16–28M)Medium
Revenue per territory~$0.9M est.Low
Adjusted EBITDA~$1.8–3.1M est. (central ~$2.6M)Low

What the numbers imply

  • At about $0.9M per territory, Punctual Pros would sit above the One Hour ($0.61M) and Ben Franklin ($0.66M) system averages. That gap is the weakest link, because it depends on the headcount input.
  • Royalty plus brand fund takes about 7.2–7.5% of revenue, roughly $1.6M est. a year. That caps adjusted EBITDA margins near 8–14% est.
  • PGIM Private Credit Fund's 10-Q for June 30, 2026 shows a first-lien loan to Punctual Pros Midco at SOFR+5.00% (8.73%), maturing Mar 26, 2029.
  • $4.83M is funded, plus a $1.4M unfunded commitment.
  • Fair value is about 98.6% of par.
  • This is one lender's disclosed position, not necessarily total debt.

Gaps and caveats

  • The verification pass on Sep 24, 2026 confirmed 29 of 30 sampled filings and removed one.
  • Actual revenue by territory and brand would replace the quartile mapping. Payroll registers would replace the wage-ratio method.
  • No public source gives the split between installation and service revenue, or membership counts.

Next actions

  1. Pull FY2025 management accounts and reconcile them to the $22M est. midpoint, by state and brand.
  2. Re-verify current headcount, since the labor cross-check rests on the unconfirmed 113 figure.
  3. Confirm the full debt stack beyond the PGIM position, including the delayed-draw terms.
  4. Benchmark revenue per territory against Authority Brands Item 19 data to test the above-system-average result.

## How the estimate is built

- **PPP base:** The Rohrer Company's April 2020 PPP loan was $745,985. That implies about $3.58M of 2019 payroll, with high confidence. It also implies about 50–58 employees and about $9–12M of 2019 revenue est. (Punctual Pros public filings).
- **Horvath base:** A $251,894 PPP loan implies about $1.21M of payroll, about 19–22 employees and about $3–4M of 2019 revenue est. (Punctual Pros public filings).
- **Labor cross-check:** About 113 employees at 2024 Lancaster wages (~$76K) and a 40–45% labor ratio imply an $18–22M PA run-rate est. at the BSP purchase on Apr 3, 2024. The 113 headcount comes from a task brief and has not been re-verified (BSP firm profile).
- **Franchise disclosure cross-check:** The 2026 franchisee lists show 25 territories, with high confidence. Mapping them to Item 19 quartiles gives about $12–19M for PA and $3–5M for NJ (Punctual Pros public filings).

## Territory and estimate summary

| Metric | Estimate | Confidence |
|---|---|---|

| Revenue per territory | ~$0.9M est. | Low |
| Adjusted EBITDA | ~$1.8–3.1M est. (central ~$2.6M) | Low |

## What the numbers imply

- At about $0.9M per territory, Punctual Pros would sit above the One Hour ($0.61M) and Ben Franklin ($0.66M) system averages. That gap is the weakest link, because it depends on the headcount input.

- PGIM Private Credit Fund's 10-Q for June 30, 2026 shows a first-lien loan to Punctual Pros Midco at SOFR+5.00% (8.73%), maturing Mar 26, 2029.
  - $4.83M is funded, plus a $1.4M unfunded commitment.
  - Fair value is about 98.6% of par.
  - This is one lender's disclosed position, not necessarily total debt.

## Gaps and caveats

- The verification pass on Sep 24, 2026 confirmed 29 of 30 sampled filings and removed one.
- Actual revenue by territory and brand would replace the quartile mapping. Payroll registers would replace the wage-ratio method.
- No public source gives the split between installation and service revenue, or membership counts.
